Patch release of the AnonRouter SDKs. It keeps Tinfoil verification current
without weakening the provider trust boundary, and corrects two Tinfoil claims
that an independent security review found to be stronger on paper than in code.

## Packages

| Package | Registry plan |
| --- | --- |
| `@anonrouter/confidential` | npm |
| `@anonrouter/client` | npm |
| `anonrouter-confidential` | GitHub wheel/sdist now; PyPI after organization approval |

The npm and PyPI jobs remain separate release switches. PyPI publication stays
off while the AnonRouter organization request is pending.

## Two corrected claims

**The TLS check compared a field to a copy of itself.** Tinfoil's verification
document reports the attested serving key twice, as
`enclaveMeasurement.tlsPublicKeyFingerprint` and as `tlsPublicKey`. Both are
copies of one field of one AMD SEV-SNP report, so requiring them to be equal
passed for every document in existence, a fabricated one included. A verdict
saying the TLS key was bound had established nothing about the connection
actually serving the route.

Both verifiers now require a transport binding recorded on a real pinned
connection, and require the certificate key observed there to equal the key in
the verified report. A document arriving without that observation fails closed.
On the client path AnonRouter's measured worker records it; in Node,
`verifyTinfoilEnclave()` records its own, so that path needs nothing from
AnonRouter at all.

**The route claimed NVIDIA evidence nobody checked.** Tinfoil verdicts reported
hardware type `amd-sev-snp+nvidia-cc`, and the copy described GPU attestation,
on a route whose official verifier establishes no NVIDIA confidential-compute
evidence. The hardware claim is now `amd-sev-snp` alone, and every Tinfoil-facing
GPU or model-weight claim is withdrawn from the packages, tests, vectors and
documentation.

## What else changed

Tinfoil rotates its signed router release more frequently than AnonRouter ships
SDK updates. The previous SDK copied each accepted release fingerprint into a
second static list, so a valid Tinfoil rollout could make its routes appear
unverified until the next AnonRouter release.

`v0.1.2` replaces that redundant list with a fixed provider-authority policy.
The official verifier must still validate the exact
`tinfoilsh/confidential-model-router` repository, tagged GitHub/Sigstore
release, AMD SEV-SNP evidence, and signed code equality with the live enclave.
Both endpoint identities the document carries must be `inference.tinfoil.sh`,
where only one was checked before. A wrong repository, unsigned or malformed
release identity, code-to-enclave mismatch, endpoint substitution, or TLS-key
substitution fails closed.

`verifyTinfoilEnclave()` is Node-only, and says so rather than degrading:
pinning the enclave's serving key means reading a peer certificate, which no
browser exposes. Importing `@anonrouter/confidential` is still browser-safe.

The Python SDK validates the same gateway-supplied document and transport
observation; Python callers who want to run Tinfoil's verifier independently can
use Tinfoil's Python client directly.

The release also refreshes AnonRouter's gateway pin to the deployed
`content-plane-v1.0.20` workload. Other providers' verification policies and
inference protocols are unchanged.

## Upgrading

No runtime export changed name or behaviour. Two TypeScript types that named
things the SDK no longer produces were removed: `TinfoilAcceptedRelease`, an
entry in the retired per-release fingerprint allowlist, replaced by
`TinfoilProviderAuthority`; and the `"amd-sev-snp+nvidia-cc"` member of
`HardwareType`, which only Tinfoil emitted and should not have. JavaScript code
that annotated a variable with either name needs a one-line edit; everything
else, including all Python code, is unaffected.

See
[`docs/release-readiness.md`](https://github.com/anonrouter/anonrouter-sdk/blob/main/docs/release-readiness.md)
for the complete gate results and limitations.
